headline: Middle East tensions spike as Trump threatens to 'obliterate' Iran, while all four big Aussie banks now expect an RBA rate hike next week — GOOG surged 2.3% last night on strong AI momentum.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: A solid night for Google last night — up 2.3% on the NASDAQ. The market is warming to Alphabet's AI story, with the newly launched Gemini 3.8 putting enterprise AI revenue back in focus. The long-term cloud and AI growth thesis remains intact.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two edged up 0.9% last night. GTA 6 anticipation continues to quietly build — Rockstar Games clarified what will happen to GTA Online after GTA VI launches, keeping the hype alive. Still sitting at a loss overall, but momentum is slowly positive.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was essentially flat last night, up just 0.1%. No major news catalysts — the stock is holding steady near all-time highs. Solid position overall, up 11.5% since purchase.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dipped another 1% at today's ASX close, continuing its rough run. No specific news today — the broader lithium sector remains under pressure as battery metal prices stay soft. This one is well down on cost (-38.7%), but no new structural bad news today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: No price data available for today's ASX session — the ETF may not have traded or data is delayed. Given last night's strong US markets (NASDAQ +1.5%, S&P +0.9%), expect VDHG to get a gentle lift when data comes through.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: No closing price data for VTS today, but last night's strong US session (S&P 500 +0.9%, NASDAQ +1.5%) is a good sign for this ETF's next update. Long-term US market exposure remains the core appeal here.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: No price data today for VGE. Emerging markets are being watched closely given Middle East escalation risks — keep an eye on oil and geopolitical developments, which can affect EM sentiment.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: No closing price data for GXAI today. The AI sector overall had a good night in the US with NASDAQ up 1.5% and GOOG jumping 2.3%, which is a positive tailwind for this ETF's underlying holdings.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike now consensus — decision next week
watch_today.detail: All four big banks — CBA, ANZ, NAB, and Westpac — now agree the RBA will raise interest rates next week. CBA economists flagged borrowers should brace for roughly a $1,464 annual increase in repayments. This doesn't directly hit your share portfolio, but rising rates tend to weigh on growth stocks and ETFs like VDHG. Worth knowing heading into next week.

watch_today.title: Middle East escalation — oil price to watch
watch_today.detail: Trump has threatened to 'obliterate' Iran as the conflict widens, and Iran is claiming the US is planning to renew a bombing campaign. Oil spiked last week but fell sharply last night (-8.2% to $92/barrel) — a big drop likely tied to ceasefire hopes or demand concerns. Volatile oil can affect inflation and market sentiment broadly. Keep watching.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Strong night, AI momentum building — hold
watch_today.detail: Google jumped 2.3% last night to $352.39 USD — your best mover. The Gemini 3.8 launch is putting enterprise AI revenue in the spotlight and the market is responding well. You're up 14.6% on this position. Nothing to do here — sit tight and let the AI story play out.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Another dip, but no new bad news — hold
watch_today.detail: Pilbara slipped another 1% today to $4.13. The position is down 38.7% overall — painful, but there's no specific new negative catalyst today. Lithium prices remain soft globally, but Pilbara is still one of Australia's largest hard-rock lithium producers. For a long-term holder, selling at these levels locks in a loss. Sit tight unless the thesis changes.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 hype quietly building — hold
watch_today.detail: Take-Two was up 0.9% last night and GTA 6 news continues to trickle positively — Rockstar clarified the future of GTA Online post-launch, keeping fan anticipation high. You're still down 10.7% overall, but the long-term thesis (GTA 6 is one of the most anticipated game releases ever) remains intact. Hold and be patient.

watch_today.title: NASDAQ +1.47% last night — good for US-exposed holdings
watch_today.detail: A solid night on Wall Street with the NASDAQ up 1.47% and S&P 500 up 0.93%. This is a tailwind for your GOOG, MSFT, TTWO positions and indirectly for VTS.AX and VDHG.AX when they update. No action needed — just good context.

world.summary: The Middle East is the dominant global story today — Trump is threatening Iran with devastating consequences as the conflict widens, oil prices are swinging wildly, and Saudi Arabia's new defence pact faces a serious test. Elsewhere, a 13-year-old Chinese swimmer stunned the world, and Trump is making major domestic policy moves.

stories.title: Trump threatens to 'obliterate' Iran as Middle East conflict escalates
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has threatened to 'obliterate' Iran as the Middle East war appears to be widening significantly. Iran is claiming the US is planning to renew a bombing campaign, and both sides are exchanging fresh warnings. The escalation comes just as the UN General Assembly is gathering in New York, making diplomatic efforts more fraught. For everyday Australians, a wider Middle East war risks pushing fuel prices back up and rattling global share markets.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia's new defence pact faces major test as Houthi conflict escalates
stories.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia recently signed a major defence pact, but the escalating conflict between Saudi-backed forces and the Houthis is putting it under immediate stress. The Houthi conflict has real consequences — it's been disrupting Red Sea shipping lanes, which pushes up the cost of goods transported between Asia and Europe, including things Australians buy. A wider regional war involving Saudi Arabia could have significant oil supply implications.

stories.title: Oil price crashes 8% as Middle East tensions create volatile swings
stories.why_it_matters: Crude oil (WTI) fell a massive 8.2% last night to $92 a barrel, down from $100.30. That's a huge single-day swing — likely driven by a mix of demand concerns and some optimism about a possible ceasefire. This is actually good news for Australian petrol prices short-term if it holds, but the volatility shows just how unstable the situation is. Oil could spike right back up if the Iran situation deteriorates.

stories.title: Trump announces major policy moves — from Greenland to drug prices
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has been rolling out a series of sweeping domestic policy announcements, reportedly spanning everything from Greenland (a long-running territorial ambition) to prescription drug pricing. The drug pricing moves could affect US pharmaceutical company profits. While the full details aren't available, the breadth of announcements signals Trump is moving aggressively on multiple fronts simultaneously, which tends to create market volatility.

stories.title: Yu Zidi, 13, wins record-breaking swimming gold — then calls it 'so-so'
stories.why_it_matters: 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi has broken a world record to claim a gold medal in a major international swimming event — then casually described her performance as 'so-so'. It's the kind of story that makes headlines globally. Yu is being compared to the prodigies of Chinese swimming's golden era, and her performance is already sparking debate about age limits and athlete development in elite sport.

markets.summary: A strong night on Wall Street last night — the NASDAQ jumped 1.47% and the S&P 500 gained 0.93%, with tech leading the charge. The big mover was oil, which cratered 8.2% amid volatile Middle East developments. Gold eased slightly. The Aussie dollar is holding steady around 71.3 US cents. ASX 200 closing data wasn't available today.

indicators.note: Good night on Wall Street last night — up 0.93%, driven by tech strength.

indicators.note: No closing data available for today's ASX session.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold eased 1% — slight retreat from recent highs but still at elevated levels historically.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar is steady, up slightly at 71.26 US cents. No major moves today.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is interest rates — all four major banks now agree the RBA will hike next week, which will hit mortgage holders hard. Meanwhile, Treasurer Jim Chalmers is hinting at tax cuts but warning of tough economic news ahead, and the Coalition is pitching petrol price relief.

stories.title: All four big banks now tipping RBA rate hike next week
stories.why_it_matters: CBA and ANZ have changed their rate forecasts, joining NAB and Westpac in predicting the Reserve Bank will lift the official interest rate at its meeting next week. CBA economists say borrowers should expect repayments to rise by roughly $1,464 per year on a typical mortgage. This is a significant shift — it means the market has gone from uncertainty to consensus on a hike. Anyone with a variable rate mortgage needs to plan for higher repayments very shortly.

stories.title: Chalmers hints at fresh tax cuts but warns of 'confronting' economic news
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has flagged he's working on fresh tax cuts but is also warning Australians to brace for 'confronting' news in the upcoming economic outlook. That's a significant mixed message — potential relief on one hand, but an admission that the economic data is going to look ugly. No specific numbers have been released yet, but the warning suggests the budget position or growth forecasts may disappoint.

stories.title: Coalition promises to cut $15 off a tank of petrol when global prices spike
stories.why_it_matters: The Coalition has announced a policy to cut $15 off the cost of a tank of petrol whenever global oil prices spike above a certain threshold. It's a direct pitch to cost-of-living pressures felt by everyday Australians. The timing is interesting given oil just crashed 8% last night — but if Middle East tensions push prices back up, this policy could become very relevant very fast. No detail yet on how the threshold would be set or funded.

ai.summary: The biggest AI story today is a bombshell lawsuit accusing OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Elon Musk's xAI of secretly agreeing to slow down AI development — essentially an antitrust case against the biggest names in the industry. Meanwhile, Albanese is in New York pitching Australia's AI credentials to Trump.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI sued over alleged secret pact to slow AI development
stories.why_it_matters: A new lawsuit filed against OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), and SpaceXAI (Elon Musk's AI company) alleges they made an illegal backroom deal to deliberately slow down AI development — essentially colluding to limit competition. The argument is that these companies publicly talk up 'AI safety' as the reason for going slow, but critics say it's actually about protecting their market positions from faster-moving rivals. If proven, this could shake up the entire AI industry and have major regulatory consequences. For GOOG holders, it's worth watching — antitrust findings could affect Google's AI strategy.

stories.title: Albanese joins AI pitch to Trump during NYC trip
stories.why_it_matters: PM Anthony Albanese is in New York for the UN General Assembly and has pivoted to join an AI investment pitch to the Trump administration. The move appears aimed at resetting what has been a mixed diplomatic trip by positioning Australia as a serious AI partner. It signals that Canberra sees AI infrastructure investment — data centres, chips, compute — as a key part of future economic diplomacy with the US.

stories.title: Australia pushes big tech for internet safety and AI regulation support
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian government is calling on big tech companies to support its push for stronger internet safety laws and AI regulation. Australia wants platforms to do more to police harmful content, and is also seeking input from tech giants on how AI should be governed. This is part of a broader global trend of governments trying to get ahead of AI before it moves faster than the law can handle — and it's directly relevant to companies like Google and Microsoft that you hold.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 3 is locked in — Dolphins host the Roosters at Suncorp on Friday night, and Panthers take on the Knights on Sunday. There was major controversy over three refereeing calls in the weekend's boilover, plus a disgraceful crowd incident where a referee was pelted with rubbish. AFL Grand Final week is here, with the Brownlow red carpet done and scalping warnings out.

stories.title: 'Penalty every day of the week': Three controversial calls seal NRL finals boilover
stories.why_it_matters: A dramatic NRL finals weekend produced a boilover, with three contentious refereeing decisions proving decisive. Pundits and fans are calling at least one of the calls 'a penalty every day of the week' — the kind of controversy that NRL fans love to argue about for days. The result sets up Finals Week 3 with the Dolphins hosting the Roosters at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night (7:50pm), and the Panthers facing the Knights at Accor Stadium on Sunday (4:00pm).

stories.title: NRL investigating after referee pelted with rubbish from crowd
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL is investigating an ugly incident during the weekend's finals match where a referee was hit by rubbish thrown from the crowd. The NRL has been cracking down hard on crowd behaviour this year, and this kind of incident will only accelerate that. Expect bans and fines for those identified.

stories.title: Finals Team Tips: Roosters missing key duo; Panthers' big Cleary reveal
stories.why_it_matters: Heading into Finals Week 3, the Roosters are sweating on two key players missing training — names not yet confirmed but described as significant. Meanwhile, there's a 'big reveal' around Panthers halfback Nathan Cleary's fitness or game plan ahead of their clash with the Knights. Both matches this weekend have serious Grand Final implications.

stories.title: AFL Grand Final week: Scalping warning and Brownlow red carpet wrap
stories.why_it_matters: AFL Grand Final week is here, with the Victorian government warning fans about ticket scalping — it's illegal in Victoria and fines can be significant. The Brownlow Medal red carpet has also been and gone, with players and their partners making headlines for their fashion choices. The Grand Final itself is the biggest single-day sporting event in Australia.
